procnotices.notice_text:
REPUBLIQUE DU NIGER

-------------------------------

Ministère de l’Education Nationale, de l’Alphabétisation et de la Promotion des Langues

-------------------------

Secrétariat Général

-------------------------------

Projet NIGER- LIRE (Learning Improvement for Results in Education)

Unité de Coordination du projet

Téléphone:+227 20 37 11 09 - Email: ucp@nigerlire.edu.ne

 

AVIS A MANIFESTATION D'INTERET RELATIF AU RECRUTEMENT D’UN(E) CONSULTANT(E) POUR CONDUIRE UNE ENQUETE DE SATISFACTION SUR LES BENEFICIAIRES DES INTERVENTIONS DU PROJET PROJET NIGER-LIRE

 

  1. Le gouvernement du Niger a reçu un don et un crédit de l’Association Internationale  de Développement (IDA) dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du Projet NIGER-LIRE (Learning Improvement for Results in Education) et se propose d’utiliser une partie de ces fonds pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat relatif au recrutement d’un (e) consultant (e) conduire une enquête de satisfaction sur les bénéficiaires des interventions du projet.
  2. Objectifs : L’enquête de satisfaction devrait permettre d’obtenir, auprès des bébéficiaires, des informations sur la pertinence et l’efficacité des interventions du projet Niger LIRE.

Plus spécifiquement, il sera question de :

  • Recueillir et analyser le niveau de satisfaction des bénéficiaires par rapport aux interventions conduites par le projet depuis son lancement ;
  • Apprécier la qualité des interventions dans le cadre de ce projet et leur plus-value sur l’amélioration des enseignements - apprentissages ;
  • Evaluer la prise en compte du genre différencié en termes de de bénéficiaires sur l’ensemble des interventions du projet ;
  • Recueillir les avis, sentiments, préoccupations et attentes, ainsi que les propositions d’amélioration des bénéficiaires, afin d’optimiser le bénéfice des interventions et appuis apportés par le Projet au sein des populations cibles
  • Formuler des recommandations pour ajuster, réorienter ou restructurer le projet pour la durée restante de mise en œuvre.
  1. Les services de consultant (« Services ») sont détaillés dans les Termes de Référence joints en annexe
  2. Résultats attendus : En lien avec les objectifs énumérés ci-dessus, les résultats suivants sont attendus de  cette enquête :
  1. Le niveau de satisfaction des bénéficiaires des interventions du projet est connu et analysé ;
  2. la qualité des interventions du projet est appréciée par les bénéficiaires ;
  3. la plus-value des interventions du projet sur l’amélioration des apprentissages est appréciée ;
  4. la prise en compte du genre dans les interventions du projet est évaluée ;
  5. des propositions d’améliorations des interventions du projet sont faites sur la base des avis, sentiments, préoccupations et attentes recueillies.
  1. Profil du consultant : L’enquête sera conduite par un(e) consultant(e), spécialisé (e) dans la conduite des enquêtes sur les bénéficiaires des actions de développement, répondant au profil suivant :
  • Être titulaire d’un diplôme universitaire de niveau BAC +5 minimum dans le domaine des sciences sociales, gestion/évaluation des projets ou toutes disciplines apparentées;
  • Avoir au moins 10 ans d’expérience dans le domaine de l’évaluation des projets de développements ;
  • avoir une expérience pertinente en matière de conduite des études d’impact et des enquêtes de satisfaction ;
  • avoir conduit au moins deux (2) missions similaires sur les cinq (5) dernières années.
  1. Durée de la prestation : La durée de la mission est de trente (30) jours à compter de la délivrance de l’ordre de service.
  2. Le dossier de candidature comprenant le Curriculum Vitae (CV) détaillé du ou de la consultant(e), mettant en exergue les expériences similaires à la mission, et doit être accompagné des diplômes requis, des attestations ou certificats de formation thématique en lien avec la mission et des attestations de bonnes fins d’exécution des contrats similaires réalisés.
  3. Le recrutement se fera suivant la méthode de sélection de consultants individuels (CI) décrite au paragraphe 7.36 et 7.37 de la Section VII du Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) de juillet 2016 révisé en novembre 2017, en août 2018, en novembre 2020, en septembre 2023, en février 2025 et septembre 2025. L’attention des consultants intéressés est attirée sur les paragraphes 3.15 à 3.16 de la Section III du Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI), relatifs aux conflits d’intérêts.
  4. Les consultants intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires à l’adresse ci-dessous du lundi au jeudi de 8 heures à 17 heures 30 minutes et le vendredi de 8 heures  à 13 heures.
  5. Dépôt des candidatures : Les dossiers de candidature rédigés en français doivent être déposées sous plis fermé à l’adresse ci-dessous, ou être transmises par voie électronique, au plus tard le 23 Mars 2026 à 17h30 mn, heure locale (GMT+1) avec mention dans l’objet : « RECRUTEMENT  D’UN(E) CONSULTANT (E) POUR CONDUIRE UNE ENQUETE DE SATISFACTION DES BENEFICIAIRES DES INTERVENTIONS DU PROJET NIGER-LIRE)».

Unité de Coordination du Projet Niger LIRE (Learning Improvement for Results in Education) Rue KK6, face espace forestier, Quartier Koira Kano, Niamey – NIGER

Téléphone : +227 20 37 11 09 / 88 15 55 55

Email : ucp@nigerlire.edu.ne ;avec copie à ayahaya@nigerlire.edu.ne ; ysouley@nigerlire.edu.ne

 

En cas de transmission électronique des dossiers de candidature et de non-confirmation de leur réception dans les 24 heures ouvrables après leur transmission, le consultant doit relancer toutes les adresses électroniques mentionnées ci-dessus pour s’en assurer. 

                                                                                    

                                                            Dr Aoula YAHAYA

 

 

Termes de référence pour le Recrutement d’un consultant pour conduire une enquête de satisfaction des Bénéficiaires des interventions du projet Niger LIRE

 

  1. Contexte et justification

L'Association Internationale de Développement (IDA - Groupe de la Banque mondiale) et l'Etat du Niger ont signé le 30 mai 2020, un accord de financement pour la mise en œuvre du Projet NIGER-LIRE (Learning Improvement for Results in Education) d’un montant global de 140 millions de USD sous forme d’un Crédit (Crédit 6572-NE de 18 200 000 Euros, soit 20 000 000 USD) et d’un Don (Don D 580-NE de 87 200 000 DTS, soit 120 000 000 USD dont 20 000 000 USD pour le volet « Réfugiés »).

Entré en vigueur le 28 septembre 2020 pour un montant initial de 140 millions USD et pour une durée de six (6) ans jusqu’au 30 avril 2026, le projet a été restructuré en 2023 et a reçu un financement additionnel de 230 millions USD avec une extension de sa date de clôture jusqu’en 2029 pour le volet « constructions scolaires ».

L'objectif de développement du projet (ODP) révisé est « Améliorer l’accès à l’éducation, la qualité des conditions d’enseignement et d’apprentissage et renforcer la planification et la gestion de l’éducation au Niger ».   

 

Le projet comprend six (6) composantes :

  • la première composante concerne l’amélioration des pratiques d’enseignement et de la pédagogie en classe ;
  • la seconde se focalise sur les interventions directes visant à améliorer l’apprentissage chez tous les enfants et à remédier aux déficits d’apprentissage les plus critiques ;
  • la troisième composante vise à renforcer les systèmes et les capacités pour la prestation de services et la gestion globale du système éducatif, notamment en intensifiant les efforts de suivi et d’évaluation des résultats d’apprentissage et du système éducatif ;
  • la quatrième composante quant à elle est axée sur l’administration de projet ;
  • la cinquième composante intitulée intervention d’urgence contingente a été ajoutée dans l’éventualité où une intervention d’urgence imprévue pourrait avoir lieu ;
  • la sixième composante est axée sur la construction des infrastructures scolaires y compris l’appui à la gestion d’internats pour les jeunes filles et concentre l’essentiel du financement additionnel.

 

La mise en œuvre technique des composantes est assurée par les Directions Centrales du Ministère en charge de l’Education Nationale, en étroite collaboration avec les structures et institutions bénéficiaires et implique une multitude de parties prenantes.

 

Afin d’assurer quotidiennement la gestion fiduciaire, le suivi-évaluation et la communication globale du projet, une unité de coordination du projet (UCP) a été mise en place par le Ministère de l’éducation nationale de l’alphabétisation et de la promotion des langues (MENAPL).    L’UCP compte 6 pôles (Gestion Financière, Passation des Marchés, Suivi-Evaluation, Infrastructures, Transformation Digitale, Sauvegardes) et est sous la tutelle du MENAPL et sous la supervision directe du Secrétaire Général dudit Ministère.

 

Au niveau régional, l’UCP assure la gestion du projet dans chacune des huit (8) régions par le biais des Unités régionales d’assistance technique (URAT). Ces URAT travaillent en étroite collaboration avec les Directions Régionales en charge de l’Éducation Nationale (DREN).

 

Sur le plan stratégique et programmatique, le Projet NIGER-LIRE contribuera à l’atteinte des résultats au niveau de l’Axe stratégique n° 2 « Développement inclusif du capital humain » du Programme de Résilience pour la Sauvegarde de la Patrie (PRSP) et son effet sectoriel 2.1 « le niveau de connaissances et d’apprentissage des populations est équitablement rehaussé ».  Il constitue à ce titre, l’un des principaux instruments de la mise en œuvre du programme éducatif du Président de la République.

Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du Plan de Travail et Budget Annuels (PTBA) dudit Projet au titre de l’année 2026, il est prévu, au niveau de la Composante 4 « Administration et gestion du projet », volet « suivi-évaluation », de conduire une enquête de satisfaction sur les bénéficiaires des interventions du projet.

Les présents TDR sont élaborés pour recruter un consultant pour conduire cette enquête.

 

 

 

 II. Objectifs :

II.1.  Objectif général

 L’objectif global est la réalisation d’une enquête de satisfaction auprès des bénéficiaires (directs et indirects) du Projet LIRE afin d’obtenir des informations sur la pertinence et l’efficacité des interventions du projet Niger LIRE.

II.2. Objectifs spécifiques 

De manière spécifique, il s’agit de :

  • Recueillir et analyser le niveau de satisfaction des bénéficiaires par rapport aux interventions conduites par le projet depuis son lancement ;
  • Apprécier la qualité des interventions dans le cadre de ce projet et leur plus-value sur l’amélioration des enseignements - apprentissages ;
  • Evaluer la prise en compte du genre différencié en termes de de bénéficiaires sur l’ensemble des interventions du projet ;

Recueillir les avis, sentiments, préoccupations et attentes, ainsi que les propositions d’amélioration des bénéficiaires, afin d’optimiser le bénéfice des interventions et appuis apportés par le Projet au sein des populations cibles.

 

  1. Résultats attendus :

      A l’issue de cette étude, les résultats suivants sont attendus :

  • Le niveau de satisfaction des bénéficiaires des interventions du projet est connu et analysé ;
  • la qualité des interventions du projet est appréciée par les bénéficiaires ;
  • la plus-value des interventions du projet sur l’amélioration des apprentissages est appréciée ;
  • la prise en compte du genre dans les interventions du projet est évaluée ;
  • des propositions d’améliorations des interventions du projet sont faites       sur la base des avis, sentiments, préoccupations et attentes recueillies.

 

  1. Livrables attendus

Le/la consultant(e) devra produire sept (7) livrables types de documents (en français) qui seront transmis à l’UCP sous format électronique :

  • Un rapport initial ou note technique présenté (e) au plus tard une semaine après la séance de cadrage. Ce rapport détaillera la compréhension de la mission, la méthodologie proposée, le cahier des besoins d’information par thématique, les questionnaires numérisés et fournira une liste indicative des acteurs à rencontrer et un programme prévisionnel ;
  • Un aide-mémoire comprenant les principales conclusions et recommandations faites par la mission. Ce document, qui constituera la base du rapport provisoire, sera présenté et remis sous format électronique à la fin de la mission de terrain ; 
  • Une base de données Excel de l’enquête avec tableau croisé dynamique des analyses sera présenté et remis sous format électronique à la fin de la mission de terrain ; 
  • Des cartes de satisfaction par thématique du projet sera présenté et remis sous format électronique à la fin de la mission de terrain ; 
  • Un rapport provisoire pour l’unité de coordination qui sera basé sur les données collectées lors de l’enquête sur le terrain à une semaine de la fin de la mission ;
  • Un rapport consolidé provisoire sera rédigé par le ou la consultant (e) à trois jours de la fin de la mission ;
  • Un rapport consolidé final sera rédigé par le/la consultant(e) en veillant à intégrer les commentaires transmis par les parties prenantes ;

 

  1. Méthodologie  

Le/la consultant(e) travaillera avec l’UCP et les structures centrales et décentralisées du MENAPL (cabinet de la ministre, secrétariat général, directions en charges de la mise en œuvre du projet, DREN) et les URATs et s’appuiera sur une base de données du pôle Suivi-Evaluation du projet. Il/elle coordonnera et harmonisera la démarche prévue.

De façon spécifique, le ou la consultant (e) définira sa méthodologie de travail qui intégrera les étapes principales suivantes mais qui ne sont pas limitatives :

  1. Séance de cadrage :  au démarrage de l’étude, le ou la Consultant (e) organisera une séance initiale de briefing avec les acteurs du projet pour clarifier les TDR et s’assurer de la bonne compréhension mutuelle des enjeux, du contenu et des modalités de la mission. La séance permettra de finaliser et valider le calendrier, ainsi que les dispositions organisationnelles et d’expliciter la méthodologie. Cette séance de cadrage permettra surtout de valider avec l’UCP les outils de collecte des données ;
  2. Validation des questionnaires : le cahier des besoins d’information nécessaire à l’atteinte des résultats de la mission et les questionnaires numérisés sur KoboCollect du projet pour des enquêtes terrains, des entretiens et interviews devront fait l’objet de validation par l’UCP.
  3. Revue documentaire : la collecte des données comprendra les principaux documents sur les priorités nationales en matière d’éducation (politiques, stratégies, …) ainsi que les plans d’action et de travail, les rapports périodiques et les études menées dans le cadre du projet, le CdR et les aide-mémoires des missions d’appui du Projet ;
  4. Enquête, Entretiens et Interviews : Les bénéficiaires directs et indirects, le personnel du ministère de tutelle et des autres ministères concernés par le projet, les membres de l’Unité de coordination du projet, les partenaires (bailleur de fonds, acteurs intervenant dans le système éducatif, entreprises, ONGs…) sont autant de sources d’informations à exploiter. Les programmes d’entretien et de visites de terrain (quand cela est possible) seront établis en concertation avec l’UCP ;
  5. Analyse et interprétations de données : l’analyse des informations de la base de données avec des tableaux croisés dynamiques devra aboutir à l’établissement de constats solides et argumentés et à la formulation de recommandations pertinentes sur chacun des points traités, diffusées après validation à tous les acteurs concernés.
  6. Cartographie des niveaux de satisfaction des thématiques phares préalablement validés par l’UCP.

 

 

  1. Ethique d’évaluation

 

Le ou la Consultant (e) devra veiller à la sauvegarde des droits et confidentialité des personnes fournissant les informations. Il devra prendre des mesures pour garantir, lorsque cela sera nécessaire, l’anonymat et la confidentialité.

 

  1. Profil du Consultant

La présente prestation sera assurée par un consultant individuel spécialisé (e) dans la conduite des enquêtes sur les bénéficiaires des actions de développement ayant au moins 10 ans d’expérience dans le domaine de l’évaluation des projets de développements avec au moins deux (2) missions similaires.

 Le consultant doit avoir le profil suivant :

  • être titulaire d’un diplôme universitaire de niveau BAC +5 minimum dans le domaine des sciences sociales, gestion/évaluation des projets ou toutes disciplines apparentées ;
  • avoir une expérience pertinente en matière de conduite des études d’impact et des enquêtes de satisfaction ;
  • avoir conduit au moins deux missions similaires sur les cinq (5) dernières années.

 

  1. Méthodes de sélection

Le consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode de consultant individuel ( CI) , conformément  au « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) » de la Banque Mondiale, adopté en Juillet 2016 et révisé en novembre 2017, Août 2018, Novembre 2020, septembre 2023, février 2025 et septembre 2025.

 

  1. Durée de la mission

La durée de la mission est de trente (30) jours à compter de la délivrance de l’ordre de service.

 

  1. Dépôt des candidatures :

Les dossiers de candidature rédigés en français doivent être déposées sous plis fermé à l’adresse ci-dessous, ou être transmises par voie électronique, au plus tard le 23 Mars 2026 à 17h30 mn, heure locale (GMT+1) avec mention dans l’objet : « RECRUTEMENT  D’UN(E) CONSULTANT (E) POUR CONDUIRE UNE ENQUETE DE SATISFACTION DES B2N2FICIAIRES DES INTERVENTIONS DU PROJET NIGER-LIRE)».

PROGRAMME ACCELERER LA GOUVERNANCE INSTITUTIONNELLE ET LES

REFORMES POUR UN FONCTIONNEMENT DURABLE DES SERVICES

Recrutement d’un consultant individuel pour l’élaboration de la stratégie de l’aide publique au développement et ses textes d’application

  1. Contexte et justification

Le gouvernement de la République du Congo a signé avec la Banque Mondiale un accord de prêt d’un montant de 70 millions USD pour le financement du Programme « accélérer la gouvernance institutionnelle et les réformes pour un fonctionnement durable des services (PAGIR) » et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce crédit pour financer les services relatifs au « Recrutement d’un consultant individuel pour l’élaboration de la stratégie de l’aide publique au développement et ses textes d’application ».

  1. Objectif de la mission

L’objectif général de l’activité est d’élaborer une stratégie de l’aide publique au développement et ses textes d’application.

De manière spécifique, il s’agit de :

  • faire le diagnostic de l’aide publique au développement ;
  • cartographier les partenaires potentiels (bilatéraux, multilatéraux, acteurs non étatiques) et définir les approches de collaboration adaptées ;
  • élaborer une stratégie alignée sur les objectifs nationaux de développement, tout en intégrant les meilleures pratiques internationales ;
  • élaborer le mécanisme de coordination de l’aide publique au développement ;
  • élaborer les outils de suivi et de gestion de l’aide publique au développement.
  1. Profil du consultant :

Le/la consultant(e) doit remplir les conditions suivantes :

  • être titulaire d’au moins un BAC + 5 en économie du développement, en relations internationales, en sciences politiques, en gestion publique, en coopération internationale, en gestion des projets ou spécialités connexes ;
  • avoir une expérience d’au moins 10 ans dans les domaines de l’économie, de la planification, de gestion axée sur les résultats, de la coopération internationale, dans la gestion des projets avec les partenaires au développement ;
  • justifier d’une expérience avérée en matière d’élaboration des stratégies et politiques de développement ;
  • avoir une expérience de gestion d’équipe ;
  • avoir des aptitudes en rédaction, en communication et en relations humaines ;
  • avoir la maîtrise des procédures et directives des partenaires techniques et financiers ;
  • avoir la maîtrise de la langue française ;
  • avoir une bonne connaissance de l’outil informatique (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.) ;
  • avoir conduit au moins trois (3) missions similaires.
  1. Durée et lieu de la mission

La mission se déroulera à Brazzaville, pour une durée de quatre (4) mois.

5.  Méthode de sélection

La sélection du consultant se fera par comparaison des CVs conformément aux procédures définies dans le Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’investissement (FPI) de la Banque mondiale, Edition de février 2025.

L’Unité de coordination du PAGIR invite les candidats à fournir, en français, un dossier de candidature comprenant un CV détaillé à jour sur support papier et/ou par voie électronique (Word ou pdf), une lettre de motivation, la photocopie des diplômes et une ou des attestations de travail.

Les candidats intéressés peuvent obtenir les termes de références de la mission tous les jours ouvrables de 9 heures à 16 heures, à l’adresse ci-dessous :

Secrétariat de l’UCP-PAGIR, A l’attention du Coordonnateur du Programme Accélérer la Gouvernance Institutionnelle et les Réformes pour un fonctionnement durable des services.  Parcelle 84 bis, avenue du Chaillu, arrondissement 3 Poto-Poto Brazzaville, République du Congo, Téléphone : (+242) 06 183 37 63, adresse électronique : pmarches@pagir.net ; secretariat@pagir.net.

Les dossiers de candidature peuvent être transmis par voie électronique ou être déposés sous plis fermés en quatre exemplaires à l'adresse ci- dessous, au plus tard le 25 Mars 2026 à 16h00 et porter clairement la mention « Recrutement d’un consultant individuel pour l’élaboration de la stratégie de l’aide publique au développement et ses textes d’application ».

 

                                                                                                      Fait à Brazzaville, le 10 mars 2026

 Le Coordonnateur,

  3. No Performance Security is required.
  4. Your bid in sealed envelope should be submitted by hand or email not later than 10:30 hours GMT of 27th March 2026 to the address below:

Freetown, Sierra Leone

procnotices.project_name: Georgia Relief and Recovery for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises
procnotices.bid_description: Provision of Consulting Services in Taxation through Consulting Centers (Growth Hubs)
procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES - FRAMEWORK AGREEMENT – SELECTION OF FIRMS)

Georgia

Project Name: The Relief and Recovery for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)

Project No: P173975

Loan No. 9239-GE

Assignment Title:  Provision of Consulting Services in Taxation through Consulting Centers (Growth Hubs)

Reference No. GE-EG-CS-QBS-2026-05

LEPL Enterprise Georgia within the Relief and Recovery for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) Project supported by the World Bank intends to apply part of the loan proceeds for consulting services in the area of Taxation. The purpose of this call is to create a qualified companies that can deliver these services.

All potential consultants which express interest to receive the Request for Proposal (RfP), will be sent the document. However, the evaluation of the submitted proposal shall be made only for those consultants, which meet the below stated evaluation criteria, and the consultants will be selected in accordance with the Framework Agreement arrangements described in the Procurement Regulations and specifically set out in the Request for Proposals (RfP). Therefore, it is advised that the potential consultants assess their profile relevance against the required criteria prior to requesting the RfP, in order to save time and resources.

The Project will be implemented nationwide and will consist of four components:

Component 1 – Financial relief and recovery for MSMEs

Component 2 – Digital payments & financial infrastructure upgrading

Component 3 – Project management and monitoring

Component 4 – Contingent Emergency Response Component

A substantial portion of the Project activities fall under Component 1. Component 1 will be implemented by LEPL Enterprise Georgia (hereinafter – Agency), which is a government economic development agency operating under the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development of Georgia. It comprises of the following sub-components:

  • Sub-component 1.1 - micro-grants to finance working capital and fixed assets for micro and small firms.
  • Sub-component 1.2 - co-finance interest payments on loans underwritten by participating financial institutions (PFIs).
  • Sub-component 1.3 - partial credit guarantees for loans issued by PFIs.
  • Sub-component 1.4 - technical assistance to MSMEs in COVID-proofing, strengthening managerial skills, and digitalization through establishing Consulting Centers in the regions of Georgia (Growth Hubs - hereinafter GHs) to deliver specific services to MSMEs locally.

The GHs established under the Sub-component 1.4 offer MSMEs three main services:

1. Consulting Services – this entails (1) identifying the problems, obstacles, and opportunities facing a specific business (hereinafter – beneficiary MSME) in terms of growth and productivity through a comprehensive diagnostic interview, (2) offering a service of a consulting company (hereinafter - Consultant) to remedy these problems and design specific solutions, and (3) co-financing the cost of this service. At the first stage, the Consulting service covers the following six areas:

  • Sales and Marketing
  • Taxation
  • Legal Issues
  • Finance and Accounting
  • Business Modeling and Strategic Planning
  • Digitalization

 

2. Improving Business Skills – this covers delivering seminars, talks, trainings, and workshops that match the needs of the businesses, organizing business meetings, and providing necessary infrastructure for these purposes.

3. Providing Information – this means providing businesses access to information about ongoing business support programs, business sector news, and the latest available research.

The consulting services (hereinafter - the Services) in the area of Taxation includes one basic package developed by the Agency with a respective list of deliverables and preliminary description of the work scope. The package is:

  • Ensuring Tax Compliance and Optimizing Taxes

 

This list can be further expended and/or modified as needed to meet any other needs of beneficiaries, provided that additional services will not go beyond the scope of services as defined in the ToR. Accordingly, upon agreement between the Consultant and the beneficiary in the Call-Off Contract, the Consultant may tailor the consulting services related to the above packages to the specific needs of the beneficiary in order to improve the packages and make them more fit to the beneficiary.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the primary procurement stage of this assignment can be found at the link below:

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Q7fmxud2bkVrTI0AltDkjPqqTaYeFHKf/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=114433811295150382465&rtpof=true&sd=true

The Agency now invites eligible consulting firms (Consultants) to indicate their interest in providing the Services in the area of Taxation. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The evaluation criteria are:

1. Registered as a business entity - in line with the Law of Georgia on Entrepreneurs, registered as a legal or individual entrepreneur, excluding the enterprises where shareholders are state or self-government authorities. (The Consultant must submit latest Extract from the Registry of Entrepreneurial and Non-entrepreneurial (Non-commercial) Legal Entities)

2. Does not have a tax debt to the state (except for the cases when the payment of the tax debt is postponed or the obligation to pay is suspended in accordance with the law); (The Consultant must submit latest Verification from the Revenue Service regarding not having tax debt to the state (or an agreement about its postponement/suspension of payment)

3. Is not registered in the Debtor Registry.

4. Is not in the process of liquidation or recognized as economically insolvent (bankrupt);

5. The Consultant has served contracts with a total value of at least 200,000 GEL within the last 3 years in the area of taxes, tax-related legal issues, regulatory compliance, or similar; (The Consultant must submit proof of completion of contract, i.e. contracts, respective delivery and acceptance certificates and payment certificates on the RfP stage). Experience in the projects relevant to the assignment should be submitted in the Form N1 on the following link: 

https://drive.google.com/file/d/1efb3T6xdt7EvotIWpGeFBN7tPpXU0-Cb/view?usp=sharing

6. Adequacy and quality of the proposed approach and methodology in responding to the Terms of Reference (details of evaluation methodology and respective scoring are indicated in the RfP) ;

7. Key Experts’ qualifications and competence for the Assignment (details of evaluation scoring are indicated in the RfP).

The potential Consultants which consider that they meet the above-mentioned qualification criteria, may submit a formal letter requesting RfP document. 

After receiving the RfP document, based on it, the Consultant shall prepare Technical Proposal and submit it to EG within the deadline indicated in the RfP.

EG will evaluate the Consultant’s qualifications and experience vis-à-vis required criteria, and if the Consultant qualify, their Technical Proposal will be evaluated as well.

Requirements for the Consultant’s Staff

In order to provide quality services Consultant should mobilize qualified personnel (key experts). The Consultant is liable for the quality of the provided Service.

List of required experts and narrative of minimum qualification requirements is given in the table below:

Expert Position (Quantity)

Minimum Specific Experience (Years)

Area of Minimum Specialization, Qualification

KEY EXPERTS

Team Leader (1)

5

At least 5 years of experience in the field, and prior experience in the management of similar projects;

Minimum Master’s degree in law, accounting, or other relevant field;

Specialist (2)

3

At least 3 years of experience in the field;

Minimum Bachelor’s degree in law, accounting, or other relevant field;

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016, revised November 2017, revised August 2018 and revised November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment: The Consultant shall not receive any remuneration in connection with the assignment except as provided in the contract. The Consultant and its affiliates shall not engage in consulting or other activities that conflict with the interest of the client under the contract. The contract shall include provisions limiting future engagement of the Consultant in other services resulting from or directly related to the firm’s consulting services in accordance with the requirements of paragraphs 3.16, 3.17 and 3.18 of the Regulations. 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

The Agency will co-finance up to 90% of the Service(s) with a maximum amount of 10,000 GEL. The cost of the Service(s) offered by the Consultant may exceed the given amount.

The Formal Letter of Expressions of Interest in English language must be submitted electronically. The Consultants are requested to clearly indicate in the letter the area of Consultancy service(s) they are applying for.

The Potential Consultants may express their interest till April 03, 2026.

Attn To: Ms. Guranda Maisuradze, Procurement Specialist

E-mail To: gmaisuradze@enterprise.gov.ge

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES - FRAMEWORK AGREEMENT – SELECTION OF FIRMS)

Georgia

Project Name: The Relief and Recovery for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)

Project No: P173975

Loan No. 9239-GE

Assignment Title:  Provision of Consulting Services in Sales and Marketing through Consulting Centers (Growth Hubs)

Reference No. GE-EG-CS-QBS-2026-01

LEPL Enterprise Georgia within the Relief and Recovery for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) Project supported by the World Bank intends to apply part of the loan proceeds for consulting services in the area of Sales and Marketing. The purpose of this call is to create a qualified companies that can deliver these services.

All potential consultants which express interest to receive the Request for Proposal (RfP), will be sent the document. However, the evaluation of the submitted proposal shall be made only for those consultants, which meet the below stated evaluation criteria, and the consultants will be selected in accordance with the Framework Agreement arrangements described in the Procurement Regulations and specifically set out in the Request for Proposals (RfP). Therefore, it is advised that the potential consultants assess their profile relevance against the required criteria prior to requesting the RfP, in order to save time and resources.

The Project will be implemented nationwide and will consist of four components:

Component 1 – Financial relief and recovery for MSMEs

Component 2 – Digital payments & financial infrastructure upgrading

Component 3 – Project management and monitoring

Component 4 – Contingent Emergency Response Component

A substantial portion of the Project activities fall under Component 1. Component 1 will be implemented by LEPL Enterprise Georgia (hereinafter – Agency), which is a government economic development agency operating under the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development of Georgia. It comprises of the following sub-components:

  • Sub-component 1.1 - micro-grants to finance working capital and fixed assets for micro and small firms.
  • Sub-component 1.2 - co-finance interest payments on loans underwritten by participating financial institutions (PFIs).
  • Sub-component 1.3 - partial credit guarantees for loans issued by PFIs.
  • Sub-component 1.4 - technical assistance to MSMEs in COVID-proofing, strengthening managerial skills, and digitalization through establishing Consulting Centers in the regions of Georgia (Growth Hubs - hereinafter GHs) to deliver specific services to MSMEs locally.

The GHs established under the Sub-component 1.4 offer MSMEs three main services:

1. Consulting Services – this entails (1) identifying the problems, obstacles, and opportunities facing a specific business (hereinafter – beneficiary MSME) in terms of growth and productivity through a comprehensive diagnostic interview, (2) offering a service of a consulting company (hereinafter - Consultant) to remedy these problems and design specific solutions, and (3) co-financing the cost of this service. At the first stage, the Consulting service covers the following six areas:

  • Sales and Marketing
  • Taxation
  • Legal Issues
  • Finance and Accounting
  • Business Modeling and Strategic Planning
  • Digitalization

 

2. Improving Business Skills – this covers delivering seminars, talks, trainings, and workshops that match the needs of the businesses, organizing business meetings, and providing necessary infrastructure for these purposes.

3. Providing Information – this means providing businesses access to information about ongoing business support programs, business sector news, and the latest available research.

The consulting services (hereinafter - the Services) in the area of Sales and Marketing include 5 basic packages developed by the Agency with respective lists of deliverables and preliminary descriptions of the work scope. These packages are:

  • Sales and Marketing System Improvement
  • Marketing Plan Development
  • Sales System Automation
  • New Market Entry (Export)
  • Launching a New Product on the Local Market

 

This list can be further expended and/or modified as needed to meet any other needs of beneficiaries, provided that additional services will not go beyond the scope of services as defined in the ToR. Accordingly, upon agreement between the Consultant and the beneficiary in the Call-Off Contract, the Consultant may tailor the consulting services related to the above packages to the specific needs of the beneficiary in order to improve the packages and make them more fit to the beneficiary.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the primary procurement stage of this assignment can be found at the link below:

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1I0RQMCsatXmdHq0uXi44sfPQnzofA68Y/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=114433811295150382465&rtpof=true&sd=true

The Agency now invites eligible consulting firms (Consultants) to indicate their interest in providing the Services in the area of Sales and Marketing. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The evaluation criteria are:

1. Registered as a business entity - in line with the Law of Georgia on Entrepreneurs, registered as a legal or individual entrepreneur, excluding the enterprises where shareholders are state or self-government authorities. (The Consultant must submit latest Extract from the Registry of Entrepreneurial and Non-entrepreneurial (Non-commercial) Legal Entities)

2. Does not have a tax debt to the state (except for the cases when the payment of the tax debt is postponed or the obligation to pay is suspended in accordance with the law); (The Consultant must submit latest Verification from the Revenue Service regarding not having tax debt to the state (or an agreement about its postponement/suspension of payment)

3. Is not registered in the Debtor Registry.

4. Is not in the process of liquidation or recognized as economically insolvent (bankrupt);

5. The Consultant has served contracts with a total value of at least 200,000 GEL within the last 3 years in the area of sales and marketing, or similar; (The Consultant must submit proof of completion of contract, i.e. contracts, respective delivery and acceptance certificates and payment certificates on the RfP stage). Experience in the projects relevant to the assignment should be submitted in the Form N1 on the following link: 

https://drive.google.com/file/d/1efb3T6xdt7EvotIWpGeFBN7tPpXU0-Cb/view?usp=sharing

6. Adequacy and quality of the proposed approach and methodology in responding to the Terms of Reference (details of evaluation methodology and respective scoring are indicated in the RfP) ;

7. Key Experts’ qualifications and competence for the Assignment (details of evaluation scoring are indicated in the RfP).

The potential Consultants which consider that they meet the above-mentioned qualification criteria, may submit a formal letter requesting RfP document. 

After receiving the RfP document, based on it, the Consultant shall prepare Technical Proposal and submit it to EG within the deadline indicated in the RFP.

EG will evaluate the Consultant’s qualifications and experience vis-à-vis required criteria, and if the Consultant qualify, their Technical Proposal will be evaluated as well.

Requirements for the Consultant’s Staff

In order to provide quality services Consultant should mobilize qualified personnel (key experts). The Consultant is liable for the quality of the provided Service.

List of required experts and narrative of minimum qualification requirements is given in the table below:

Expert Position (Quantity)

Minimum Specific Experience (Years)

Area of Minimum Specialization, Qualification

KEY EXPERTS

Team Leader (1)

5

At least 5 years of experience in the field, and prior experience in the management of similar projects;

Minimum Master’s degree in marketing, business management, or other relevant field;

Specialist (2)

3

At least 3 years of experience in the field;

Minimum Bachelor’s degree in marketing, business management, or other relevant field;

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016, revised November 2017, revised August 2018 and revised November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment: The Consultant shall not receive any remuneration in connection with the assignment except as provided in the contract. The Consultant and its affiliates shall not engage in consulting or other activities that conflict with the interest of the client under the contract. The contract shall include provisions limiting future engagement of the Consultant in other services resulting from or directly related to the firm’s consulting services in accordance with the requirements of paragraphs 3.16, 3.17 and 3.18 of the Regulations. 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

The Agency will co-finance up to 90% of the Service(s) with a maximum amount of 10,000 GEL. The cost of the Service(s) offered by the Consultant may exceed the given amount.

The Formal Letter of Expressions of Interest in English language must be submitted electronically. The Consultants are requested to clearly indicate in the letter the area of Consultancy service(s) they are applying for.

The Potential Consultants may express their interest till April 03, 2026.

Attn To: Ms. Guranda Maisuradze, Procurement Specialist

E-mail To: gmaisuradze@enterprise.gov.ge

procnotices.notice_text:
TÜRKİYE FLOOD AND DROUGHT MANAGEMENT PROJECT (P179313)

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST FOR PROCUREMENT SPECIALIST

The Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry (MoAF) of Türkiye, Directorate General of Water Management (GDWM) has received financing from the World Bank (“the Bank”) toward the cost of the Türkiye Flood and Drought Management Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

DGWM serves as the co-implementing agency for the Project. The overall objective of the Project is to support climate change projections, determine their impacts on scenario-specific flood and drought disasters, and improve and expand existing early warning systems. It aims to strengthen the technical and operational capacities of all stakeholders for the uninterrupted and effective operation of the system.

DGWM has established a Project Implementation Unit (PIU) within its administrative structure to manage the project activities. DGWM intends to engage a Procurement Specialist (individual consultant) to provide technical support to the DGWM PIU in managing procurement activities under the Project. The Procurement Specialist will be responsible for planning and providing procurement services, including preparing procurement plans, bidding documents, evaluation reports, training activities and monitoring contract performance.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR), including the qualification requirements and scope of work for the assignment, can be found at the following web page address: https://www.tarimorman.gov.tr/SYGM/Sayfalar/Detay.aspx?SayfaId=187

Hiring Methodology

The Procurement Specialist will be selected through the ‘Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants’ method in accordance with the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (September 2023)”. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations setting forth the World Bank’s policy on Conflict of Interest.

Individuals currently working as procurement consultants on another World Bank-financed project may also compete, provided they meet the requirements for early termination of their existing contracts to avoid disruption in project implementation.

Duration and Place of Work

The Procurement Specialist is expected to commence work in April 2026 with a 6-month contract having a two-month probation period. The Procurement Specialist will work on a full-time basis and will be located in Ankara, with potential travel to project sites as required.

Application Procedure

Interested eligible candidates should submit their CVs in both English and Turkish (in the format specified on the website), clearly indicating the position title and the reference number TR-DGWM-541747-CS-INDV in the subject line.

Applications must be delivered in PDF format via e-mail to the address below no later than March 30, 2026, at 16:00 (local time).

Contact Information:

Directorate General of Water Management (GDWM)

Attn: Cihat Adsız

E-mail: cihat.adsiz@tarimorman.gov.tr

Web Site: https://www.tarimorman.gov.tr/SYGM/Sayfalar/Detay.aspx?SayfaId=186

PROJETO COOPERAR DO ESTADO DA PARAÍBA


 

SOLICITAÇÃO DE MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE


 

Contratação de Consultoria Individual – Pessoa Física especializada para a implantação da nova versão do sistema Solução Online de Licitação - SOL, com a alteração da linguagem em “Ruby on Rails” para JAVA, visando adequar o fluxo de funcionamento do SOL 2.0 para os PROJETOS BAHIA QUE PRODUZ E ALIMENTA (BA) e PARAIBA RURAL SUSTENTÁVEL (PB)


 

Acordo de Empréstimo N. º 8639-BR

Método:  Seleção de Consultoria Individual – SCI nº 001/2026


 

Prezado Senhor,


 

1. O Governo do Estado da Paraíba firmou um empréstimo com o Banco Internacional para Reconstrução e Desenvolvimento – BIRD – para financiar o PB Rural Sustentável e pretende utilizar parte do montante de pagamento para Contratação de Consultoria Individual – Pessoa Física especializada para a implantação da nova versão do sistema Solução Online de Licitação - SOL, com a alteração da linguagem em “Ruby on Rails” para JAVA, visando adequar o fluxo de funcionamento do SOL 2.0 para os PROJETOS BAHIA QUE PRODUZ E ALIMENTA (BA) e PARAIBA RURAL SUSTENTÁVEL (PB), em conformidade com o Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários de Operações de Financiamento de Projetos de Investimento – Acordo de Empréstimo 8639 – BR.


2. O Projeto Cooperar do Estado da Paraíba – Cooperar-PB, através da Comissão Especial de Licitação – CEL, convida Vossa Senhoria a manifestar seu interesse na prestação dos serviços requeridos. A contratação será pelo método de Seleção de Consultoria Individual para a implantação da nova versão do sistema Solução Online de Licitação - SOL, com a alteração da linguagem em “Ruby on Rails” para JAVA, visando adequar o fluxo de funcionamento do SOL 2.0 para os PROJETOS BAHIA QUE PRODUZ E ALIMENTA (BA) e PARAIBA RURAL SUSTENTÁVEL (PB), de acordo com os procedimentos estabelecidos pelo Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários de Operações de Financiamento de Projetos de Investimentos – Banco Mundial. 

 

3. Serão consideradas as Manifestações de Interesse que atendam aos seguintes requisitos de experiência e qualificação:

∙ Formação superior em Análise de Sistemas, Sistemas de Informação, Design Gráfico ou similares;

∙ Experiência em desenvolvimento de sistemas utilizando as linguagens JAVA, Vue Js;

∙ Conhecimento em Implantação de ambiente Docker;

∙ Conhecimento do framework Quasar;

∙ Conhecimento de banco de Dados POSTGRESQL;

∙ Conhecimento em Gestão de Processos de T.I.

 

A documentação comprobatória (currículo e atestados de capacidade técnica) deverá ser apresentada para todos os critérios avaliados.


 4. A sua manifestação de interesse pressupõe compromisso de contratação, para tanto, solicitamos o envio de currículo profissional para o e-mail: pbruralcpl@gmail.com.

 

 5. O currículo deverá, impreterivelmente, ser enviado até às 23h:59min do dia 26 de março de 2026.

 

 6. Esta Solicitação de Manifestação de Interesse e o Termo de Referência poderão ser visualizados no seguinte endereço: www.cooperar.pb.gov.br/downloads.



 

João Pessoa/PB, 04 de março de 2026.

                                                   


Omar José Batista Gama

Coordenador Geral do Projeto Cooperar

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES - FRAMEWORK AGREEMENT – SELECTION OF FIRMS)

 

Georgia

Project Name: The Relief and Recovery for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)

Project No: P173975

Loan No. 9239-GE

Assignment Title:  Provision of Consulting Services in Legal Issues through Consulting Centers (Growth Hubs)

Reference No. GE-EG-CS-QBS-2026-04

LEPL Enterprise Georgia within the Relief and Recovery for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) Project supported by the World Bank intends to apply part of the loan proceeds for consulting services in the area of Legal Issues. The purpose of this call is to create a qualified companies that can deliver these services.

All potential consultants which express interest to receive the Request for Proposal (RfP), will be sent the document. However, the evaluation of the submitted proposal shall be made only for those consultants, which meet the below stated evaluation criteria, and the consultants will be selected in accordance with the Framework Agreement arrangements described in the Procurement Regulations and specifically set out in the Request for Proposals (RfP). Therefore, it is advised that the potential consultants assess their profile relevance against the required criteria prior to requesting the RfP, in order to save time and resources.

The Project will be implemented nationwide and will consist of four components:

Component 1 – Financial relief and recovery for MSMEs

Component 2 – Digital payments & financial infrastructure upgrading

Component 3 – Project management and monitoring

Component 4 – Contingent Emergency Response Component

A substantial portion of the Project activities fall under Component 1. Component 1 will be implemented by LEPL Enterprise Georgia (hereinafter – Agency), which is a government economic development agency operating under the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development of Georgia. It comprises of the following sub-components:

  • Sub-component 1.1 - micro-grants to finance working capital and fixed assets for micro and small firms.
  • Sub-component 1.2 - co-finance interest payments on loans underwritten by participating financial institutions (PFIs).
  • Sub-component 1.3 - partial credit guarantees for loans issued by PFIs.
  • Sub-component 1.4 - technical assistance to MSMEs in COVID-proofing, strengthening managerial skills, and digitalization through establishing Consulting Centers in the regions of Georgia (Growth Hubs - hereinafter GHs) to deliver specific services to MSMEs locally.

The GHs established under the Sub-component 1.4 offer MSMEs three main services:

1. Consulting Services – this entails (1) identifying the problems, obstacles, and opportunities facing a specific business (hereinafter – beneficiary MSME) in terms of growth and productivity through a comprehensive diagnostic interview, (2) offering a service of a consulting company (hereinafter - Consultant) to remedy these problems and design specific solutions, and (3) co-financing the cost of this service. At the first stage, the Consulting service covers the following six areas:

  • Sales and Marketing
  • Taxation
  • Legal Issues
  • Finance and Accounting
  • Business Modeling and Strategic Planning
  • Digitalization

2. Improving Business Skills – this covers delivering seminars, talks, trainings, and workshops that match the needs of the businesses, organizing business meetings, and providing necessary infrastructure for these purposes.

3. Providing Information – this means providing businesses access to information about ongoing business support programs, business sector news, and the latest available research.

The consulting services (hereinafter - the Services) in the area of Legal Issues include 2 basic packages developed by the Agency with respective lists of deliverables and preliminary descriptions of the work scope. These packages are:

  • Support in Regulatory Compliance
  • Preparing Templates for Contracts

 

This list can be further expended and/or modified as needed to meet any other needs of beneficiaries, provided that additional services will not go beyond the scope of services as defined in the ToR. Accordingly, upon agreement between the Consultant and the beneficiary in the Call-Off Contract, the Consultant may tailor the consulting services related to the above packages to the specific needs of the beneficiary in order to improve the packages and make them more fit to the beneficiary.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the primary procurement stage of this assignment can be found at the link below:

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1FqP9HPyX9sqnl8ofevtl1RklnZhQmKDx/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=114433811295150382465&rtpof=true&sd=true

The Agency now invites eligible consulting firms (Consultants) to indicate their interest in providing the Services in the area of Legal Issues. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The evaluation criteria are:

1. Registered as a business entity - in line with the Law of Georgia on Entrepreneurs, registered as a legal or individual entrepreneur, excluding the enterprises where shareholders are state or self-government authorities.  (The Consultant must submit latest Extract from the Registry of Entrepreneurial and Non-entrepreneurial (Non-commercial) Legal Entities)

2. Does not have a tax debt to the state (except for the cases when the payment of the tax debt is postponed or the obligation to pay is suspended in accordance with the law); (The Consultant must submit latest Verification from the Revenue Service regarding not having tax debt to the state (or an agreement about its postponement/suspension of payment)

3. Is not registered in the Debtor Registry.

4. Is not in the process of liquidation or recognized as economically insolvent (bankrupt);

5. The Consultant has served contracts with a total value of at least 200,000 GEL within the last 3 years in the area of law, business-related legal issues, regulatory compliance, or similar; (The Consultant must submit proof of completion of contract, i.e. contracts, respective delivery and acceptance certificates and payment certificate on the RfP stage). Experience in the projects relevant to the assignment should be submitted in the Form N1 on the following link: 

https://drive.google.com/file/d/1efb3T6xdt7EvotIWpGeFBN7tPpXU0-Cb/view?usp=sharing

6. Adequacy and quality of the proposed approach and methodology in responding to the Terms of Reference (details of evaluation methodology and respective scoring are indicated in the RfP) ;

7. Key Experts’ qualifications and competence for the Assignment (details of evaluation scoring are indicated in the RfP).

The potential Consultants which consider that they meet the above-mentioned qualification criteria, may submit a formal letter requesting RfP document. 

After receiving the RfP document, based on it, the Consultant shall prepare Technical Proposal and submit it to EG within the deadline indicated in the RFP.

EG will evaluate the Consultant’s qualifications and experience vis-à-vis required criteria, and if the Consultant qualify, their Technical Proposal will be evaluated as well.

Requirements for the Consultant’s Staff

In order to provide quality services Consultant should mobilize qualified personnel (key experts). The Consultant is liable for the quality of the provided Service.

List of required experts and narrative of minimum qualification requirements is given in the table below:

Expert Position (Quantity)

Minimum Specific Experience (Years)

Area of Minimum Specialization, Qualification

KEY EXPERTS

Team Leader (1)

5

At least 5 years of experience in the field, and prior experience in the management of similar projects;

Minimum Master’s degree in law or other relevant field;

Specialist (2)

3

At least 3 years of experience in the field;

Minimum Bachelor’s degree in law or other relevant field;

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016, revised November 2017, revised August 2018 and revised November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment: The Consultant shall not receive any remuneration in connection with the assignment except as provided in the contract. The Consultant and its affiliates shall not engage in consulting or other activities that conflict with the interest of the client under the contract. The contract shall include provisions limiting future engagement of the Consultant in other services resulting from or directly related to the firm’s consulting services in accordance with the requirements of paragraphs 3.16, 3.17 and 3.18 of the Regulations. 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

The Agency will co-finance up to 90% of the Service(s) with a maximum amount of 10,000 GEL. The cost of the Service(s) offered by the Consultant may exceed the given amount.

The Formal Letter of Expressions of Interest in English language must be submitted electronically. The Consultants are requested to clearly indicate in the letter the area of Consultancy service(s) they are applying for.

The Potential Consultants may express their interest till April 03, 2026.

Attn To: Ms. Guranda Maisuradze, Procurement Specialist

E-mail To: gmaisuradze@enterprise.gov.ge

Request for Quotation

SUPPLY AND DELIVERY OF EQUIPMENT (TABLET & GPS/ GNSS) FOR FIELD WORK
  1. The Government of Sierra Leone (hereinafter referred to as “The Borrower”) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Project Preparation Advances. The Borrower through the Sierra Leone Land Administration Project of the Ministry of Lands Housing and Country Planning (MLHCP) intends to apply part of the proceeds of the funds for eligible payments under the contracts, subject to this Request for Quotation (RFQ).
  2. The SLLAP therefore solicits your quotation for the item as stated in the attached Annex 2. Please quote your delivery unit and total prices and state your earliest delivery time.
  3. No Performance Security is required.
  4. Your bid in sealed envelope should be submitted by hand or email not later than 10:30 hours GMT of 26th March 2026 to the address below:

  Sierra Leone Land Administration Project (SLLAP)

West Wing of 3rd Floor, Youyi Building, Brookfield’s.

Freetown, Sierra Leone

Attention: The Procurement Specialist

      Email: sllapprocurement79@gmail.com

The inner and outer envelopes shall:

  1. bear the name and address of the Bidder;
  2. be addressed to the Employer as indicated above;
  3. bear the specific identification (Title and Reference Number) of this bidding process indicated above; and
  4. bear a warning not to open before the time and date for bid opening.
  1. Your quotation must be valid for 45 days and written in English.
  2. Criteria for award will be prices, delivery time, quality and adherence to specifications.
  3. SLLAP payment terms for this contract are 100% payment upon delivery by cheque not later than 30 days after receipt and acceptance of goods and original invoice(s) by the end user department.
  4. You will be required to deliver the item not later than 15 working days from the time of notification of the award/purchase order, if your quotation is considered successful.
  5. Queries arising from this RFQ should be sent in writing or email to the address in Paragraph D above for the attention of the Procurement Management Specialist, not later than 09:00 hours of 26th March, 2026. You are requested to quote your delivered price for these items by completing and returning Annexes 1 and 2.
  6. Quotations and supporting documents as specified in Annex 1 (if any) must be marked with the Reference Number above and indicate your acceptance of the terms and conditions of this RFQ.
  7. The attached Schedule of Requirement in Annex 2 details the items to be purchased. You are requested to quote your delivery price for this item by completing and returning Annexes 1 and 2

       The address for delivery of the goods is:

       Sierra Leone Land Administration Project (SLLAP)

West Wing of 3rd Floor, Youyi Building, Brookfield’s.

Freetown, Sierra Leone

Attention: The Procurement Specialist

Request for Quotation of SUPPLY AND DELIVERY OF EQUIPMENT (TABLET & GPS/ GNSS) FOR FIELD WORK

 RFQ/ SL-MLHCP-540446-GO-RFQ - 12/03/2026

Item No

Items
 

Specification

Quantity

Delivered Unit Price (SLL)

Delivered Total Price (SLL)

1

Tablets for Field Work and Trainings

Display & Input

Screen: 10”–12” FHD+ (16:10 ratio); 800+ nits sunlight-readable with anti-glare.

Touch: Multi-touch (glove/wet finger) + Active Stylus (Wacom/EMR/USI) for precise drawing.

GPS & Positioning    

Built-in GPS preferable (5-10m standalone accuracy acceptable, used primarily for navigation and cross-referencing with handheld GPS for mapping measurements). It must be possible to connect to a separate high accuracy GNSS antenna (see specifications under GNSS) and perform GNSS measurements by using the QField mapping software installed in the tablet. The external GNSS antenna should be integrated in the mapping functions so that it is possible to switch between image delineation and external GNSS antenna measurements.

It is of high importance that the field tablet and GNSS antenna have integrated functionality so that it is possible to use the image for delineation in QField in the tablet, and then (within the same parcel surveying) be able to switch to the high precision GNSS antenna if the boundary vertice (as indicated on the ground by the land holder) is not visible in the image.

Hardware: 16GB RAM minimum; Intel Core i5 (8th Gen+) or equivalent ARM. 256GB+ SSD (micro SD expandable). 8–10 hours’ life; hot-swappable; supports solar/PD charging (18W+).

GIS & Connectivity

Mapping: Internal GPS for approximate location (5-10m) + support for high-accuracy external GNSS (via QField).

Network: 4G LTE/5G compatible with Sierra Leone networks (Orange/One Mobile); Wi-Fi & Bluetooth.

Software: Supports SL coordinate systems (WGS84 UTM 28N/29N) and standard layers (SHP, KML, Geo TIFF).

Ruggedness & OS

Durability: IP67 rating; MIL-STD-810G/H; 1.2m drop resistance onto concrete.

Environment: Operating range 0°C to 50°C; lightweight (<1.5kg).

OS: Windows 10/11 Pro (for full desktop GIS and Support for stylus-based drawing and annotation in GIS applications. OS update/support lifecycle: Windows: Security updates supported through at least 2028.

       35

  

     

2

GPS / GNSS - Equipment Sets

Core requirement: The GNSS should be able to connect to / use the field tablet (as specified under the tablet item) as software panel. It should be possible to perform GNSS measurements (as per the accuracy demands specified below) by using the QField mapping software in the field tablet.

Operational: Must support NTRIP Client protocol for connection to the Sierra Leone CORS Network. Real-Time Kinematic (RTK) for immediate precision and Post-Processed Kinematic (PPK) as a redundancy for areas with poor cellular coverage. Hardware is open-format (RTCM 3.x) to be compatible with CORS signals. The receiver must be capable of broadcasting NMEA data over Bluetooth to the field tablet, ensuring seamless position override within the QField application; Multi-constellation, RTK/CORS capable;

Data Management & Storage: Minimum 8GB for raw observation logging (essential for PPK backup). Direct export or software conversion to SHP, DXF, KML, and CSV; Full support for WGS84 UTM Zone 28N and 29N (Sierra Leone’s primary zones) and the ability to upload custom Local Grid transformation parameters.

Communication & User Interface: Bluetooth 4.0 (Dual mode) for tablet connection; Wi-Fi 802.11n for network tethering/NTRIP. USB-C for fast data transfer and charging; the receiver should have LED indicators for: Power, Satellite Tracking, Correction Signal, and Bluetooth Status.

Physical: IP67 (Dustproof; waterproof immersion up to 1m). Industrial grade (suitable for tropical climates). Maximum 1.5 kg (including battery) to ensure user comfort during long field days. Designed for one-handed operation with secure strap attachments.

Power System: Minimum 10 hours of active RTK/CORS tracking. Hot-swappable lithium-ion batteries. Each unit must include one internal battery plus one spare battery as a standard set.

Mounting & Safety: Non-metallic (Fiberglass or Carbon Fiber). This is a critical safety requirement for Sierra Leone’s rainy season to minimize lightning conductivity. Telescopic or sectional; adjustable from 1.2m to 2.0m. standard 5/8" threaded stud for receiver; includes a rugged tablet bracket.

10

 

 

3

QField licenses

QField Cloud subscriptions for 115 users (specify plan type: Pro plan €12/month per user OR Organization plan €16/user/month).

For enabling partially online work QField Cloud needs to get as a separate paid subscription for teams’ collaboration. If procurement is for support/training instead, specify: “QField deployment, training, and support services for 115 users” QField (the mobile app) is free and open source (GPL v2+), but only up to limited number of users.

35

 

 

 

TOTAL

procnotices.bid_description: Hiring of HR Firm for deployment of Staff at Healthcare Facilities of Project Districts
procnotices.contact_organization: Project Management Unit of Health Department
procnotices.notice_text:
Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa

                                                         Health Department

Request for Expression of Interest

for   

Hiring of HR Firm for deployment of Staff at Healthcare Facilities of Project Districts.

Country: Pakistan

Name of Project: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Human Capital Investment Project (KP-HCIP).

Contract Title:  Hiring of HR Firm for deployment of Staff at Healthcare Facilities of Project Districts.

CS Reference No.:  PK-HPMU-526587-CS-QCBS

Market Approach.: Open International

Duration of the Assignment: 06 months.

Project ID: PR2010039, Grant No: D680-PK, Credit Number: 6714-PK

BACKGROUND

The Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Human Capital Investment Project (KP-HCIP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include recruitment, deployment, and management of qualified healthcare personnel to support BEmONC-designated health facilities in the districts of Peshawar, Swabi, Haripur, and Nowshera. The assignment will be completed within Six (06) months after the signing of the contract and shall include:

  • Recruitment and deployment of qualified healthcare staff at designated BHUs/RHCs to ensure availability of maternal, newborn, and child health services.
  • Organizing orientation and training for deployed staff in accordance with approved clinical protocols and government guidelines.
  • Providing supportive supervision, clinical mentorship, and coordination with district health authorities and facility management.
  • Managing human resource administration, including payroll processing, attendance monitoring, and replacement of staff when required.
  • Monitoring staff performance and service delivery, maintaining records, and submitting regular progress and performance reports.

The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below or downloaded from https://www.healthkp.gov.pk/

The Project Management Unit (PMU) of KP-HCIP now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

SHORTLISTING CRITERIA

The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. General experience in the health sector, including at least five (05) years of experience in training programs, health operations, or institutional setup in line with ToRs.
  2. Experience in at least two (02) similar assignments of comparable complexity involving clinical and/or public health trainings for government or donor-funded projects. Relevant contracts or completion certificates must be provided in line with ToRs.
  3. Experience working with government institutions and/or development partners, including familiarity with donor-funded project implementation arrangements.
  4. Demonstrated technical, managerial, and organizational capacity to undertake the assignment.
  5. Technical and logistical capacity to implement training activities across multiple districts.

Detailed evaluation of financial capacity, staffing arrangements, and proposed key experts will be carried out at the Request for Proposals (RFP) stage.

KEY ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS:

Consulting firms from all countries are eligible in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (July 2016, revised November 2017, July 2018, November 2020, September 2023, February 2025 and September 2025).

  1. Firms may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications in the form of a joint venture or sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all partners shall be jointly and severally liable for the contract.
  2. Firms must demonstrate adequate organizational and institutional capacity to undertake the assignment.
  3. Availability of appropriate human resources should be demonstrated; detailed CVs will be requested at the RFP stage.
  4. Local firms must provide legal registration in Pakistan with valid NTN and KPRA registration.
  5. Foreign firms will be required to obtain relevant local registrations prior to contract award, not at the Expression of Interest stage.

 

SELECTION METHOD

A Consulting Firm will be selected in accordance with the Quality- and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method with market approach of open international as per the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, July 2016, revised November 2017, July 2018, November 2020, September 2023, February 2025 and September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”). Conflict of Interest provisions under paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the Regulations shall apply.

 

Firms that are shortlisted based on this REOI will be invited to submit detailed technical and financial proposals through a Request for Proposals (RFP). The final selection will be made based on the evaluation of these proposals to identify the most advantageous offer in terms of quality and cost.

 

SUBMISSION OF EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

  1. Interested firms may obtain additional information from the address below during office hours (0900–1600 hrs).
  2. EOIs must be submitted in hard copy to the address below on or before:
    09 April 2026 at 11:00 AM.  Late submissions will not be accepted.
     

EOIs must be submitted in a sealed envelope clearly marked:
“Expression of Interest’’

Hiring of HR Firm for deployment of Staff at Healthcare Facilities of Project Districts

(QCBS).

 

Project Director, KP-HCIP (Health)
Health Department, Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
House No. 240, Defence Officers Colony, Shami Road, Peshawar, Pakistan

Email Adress: kphciphealth163@gmail.com

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REoI)

 

(INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT)

 

CONSULTANT SERVICE FOR DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION OF

COMPETENCY-BASED RECRUITMENT MODEL

 

Country:                         Kingdom of Lesotho

Project :                            Public Sector Foundations for Services Delivery Project (P174171)

Loan No.:                       74920 -LS

Assignment Title:             Consultant Service for Design and Implementation of

    Competency-Based Recruitment Model

Activity Reference No.:    LS-MOFDP-534604-CS-INDV

Issue Date:                     February 24, 2026

 

The Kingdom of Lesotho through the Ministry of Finance and Development Planning (MoFDP) has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Public Sector Foundations for Service Delivery Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for procurement of consulting services for Consultant Service for Design and Implementation of Competency-Based Recruitment Model.

The Consultant Service for Design and Implementation of Competency-Based Recruitment Model consulting services (“the Services “) include to:

  1. Develop a competency-based recruitment model aligned with the PSC’s mandate.
  2. Incorporate all relevant legal, regulatory, and policy frameworks to ensure fairness, transparency, and consistency.
  3. Establish a system that reliably identifies the competencies, skills, and attributes required for effective performance in public service roles.
  4. Develop standardized tools and guidelines, including competency-based interviews and assessments.
  5. Build the capacity of PSC Commissioners and Secretariat staff to implement competency-based recruitment processes.

The duration of the assignment is four (4) months

The expected commencement date is June 01, 2026.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be accessed at the following website: Tenders - Government of Lesotho

or

can be obtained at the address given below.

or

by sending a request to the email addresses below.

The Ministry of Finance and Development Planning now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (attach curriculum vitae with description of experience in similar assignments, similar conditions, etc.). Firms’ staff may express interest through the employing firm for the assignment and, under such situation, only the experience and qualifications of individuals shall be considered in the selection process.

 

The criteria for selecting the Consultant are:

  1. Academic Qualifications
  • Master’s Degree in either Human Resources Management, Organizational Development, or Industrial Psychology.

 

  1. Professional Experience
  • Minimum of fifteen (15) years of professional experience in HRM reforms, recruitment system design, or public sector HR modernization.
  • Demonstrated expertise in competency modelling, job profiling, and assessment tool development.
  • Experience conducting organizational assessments and benchmarking.
  • Evidence of prior assignment(s) involving public sector reforms including the development of competency frameworks/models, preferably in Sub-Saharan Africa.
  • Experience delivering capacity-building and training programs for senior government stakeholders.

 

  1. Knowledge and Communication Skills
  • Strong analytical, facilitation, and communication skills.
  • Excellent report writing, ability to work with high-level stakeholders

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Fifth edition, September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with Individual Consultant Selection (INDV) method as set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 0900 to 1600 hours.

 

Expressions of interest must be submitted not later than 4:00 pm on March 13, 2025 in a written form as follows:

 

  • Hard copies - 1 Original and five (5) copies

       Or

  • Submit by e-mail at the email addresses provided below.

Submissions must be clearly titled (including on the submission envelope where applicable): Consultant Service for Design and Implementation Competency-Based Recruitment Model.

 

In case of hand delivery, the submissions must be delivered at the address below.
